args.rationale: SCENARIO 1 – Ohio suit against Karvella Presses LLC (Indiana company with principal place of business in Fort Wayne, IN). General jurisdiction: Karvella is not domiciled in Ohio (a corporation is at home in its state of incorporation and its principal place of business state, both in Indiana), so general jurisdiction is unavailable. Specific jurisdiction requires BOTH prongs. Prong (a) purposeful contacts: Karvella's sales director traveled to Ohio six separate times over eight months to demonstrate press models on Ostrander's Canton floor, negotiate terms, and Karvella signed the supply contract at Ostrander's Canton offices. This is precisely the repeated-travel-to-solicit-and-negotiate-the-contract-being-sued-upon conduct the memo holds satisfies purposeful availment; these contacts are not unilateral acts by the plaintiff nor fortuitous transit. Prong (a) satisfied. Prong (b) nexus: the claim — Karvella's failure to deliver the very presses ordered under the supply contract — arises directly out of the contract that was negotiated and signed in Ohio (these very forum contacts). Prong (b) satisfied. Because both prongs of the specific jurisdiction test are met, under the operative memo's test an Ohio court HAS personal jurisdiction over Karvella in Scenario 1. APPROVED.
